question: A man covers a certain distance at a speed of 60 km/h and returns at a speed of 40 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Average speed = 2ab/(a + b)

Where a and b is speed

⇒ (2 times 60 times 40) over 60 + 40 = 48 km/h

**∴ Average speed is 48 km/h**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

Certain distance at a speed = 60 km/h 

Returns of same distance at a speed = 40 km/h

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Calculation:**

Let distance = a km

⇒ Time = a/60 h

⇒ Time taken on return = a/40

⇒ Total distance = a + a = 2a

Total time taken = a/60 + a/40

⇒ (2a + 3a) / 120

⇒ 5a/120

⇒ a/24

Average speed = 2a times 24over a = 48 km/h

∴ Average speed is 48 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**If both direction cover same distance then use,

Average speed = 2ab/(a + b)

Where a and b is speed

Otherwise go with alternate solution.
